title: Basic types
explain: TypeScript adds types to JavaScript so many mistakes are caught before the code runs. The basic types are `string`, `number`, `boolean`, arrays like `string[]`, and `any`, which turns checking off. Most of the time you can let TypeScript infer the type and only annotate where it cannot.
exercise: Declare a variable for a score and another for a list of names, then assign the wrong type to each and read the error messages.
tip: `any` switches off type checking for that value. Use `unknown` when you really don't know the type, and check it before you use it.
